# Foil Reel Mounting Device

The foil reel mounting device is designed to support a reel of stamping foil within a supporting module to which it is securely fixed. This arrangement ensures that the reel remains stable and properly positioned during operation.

## Device Structure

At the core of the device is a support featuring a recess specifically designed to receive the axle of the stamping foil reel. This recess provides a secure seating point for the axle, allowing the reel to be held reliably in place.

## Retaining Mechanism

A retaining element is mounted on the support and can move between two distinct positions:

- A **closed position**, in which the axle is held securely within the recess, and
- An **open position**, in which the axle is released, permitting removal or replacement of the reel.

To enhance ease of use and operational reliability, the retaining element is biased towards the closed position. This biasing arrangement enables the reel to be secured automatically once the axle is seated, without requiring additional manual intervention.

## Scope of the Invention

Beyond the mounting device itself, the invention also encompasses:

- A **supporting module** incorporating the device,
- A **stamping machine** that integrates the device, and
- A **method** for loading and unloading the reel.

Together, these aspects provide a comprehensive solution for the efficient and secure handling of stamping foil reels within a stamping machine.

# Foil Reel Mounting Device for Stamping Foil Applications

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to the field of stamping and printing equipment, and more particularly to a foil reel mounting device designed to support a stamping foil reel within a supporting module. The invention further extends to supporting modules incorporating such a device, as well as to stamping machines equipped with these components.

## Background

In modern stamping and hot-foil printing operations, stamping foil is commonly supplied in the form of a reel that must be mounted onto a supporting structure prior to use. The reel is typically wound around a central axle, which serves as the rotational axis about which the foil unwinds during operation. As the stamping process consumes the foil, spent reels must be removed and replaced with fresh material.

Conventional mounting arrangements often require operators to manually thread the axle through mounting brackets or to engage complex locking mechanisms, procedures that can be time-consuming and prone to error. The frequent interruptions necessary for reel replacement can significantly reduce the overall productivity of a stamping machine. Accordingly, there exists a need for a mounting device that facilitates the rapid and reliable loading and unloading of stamping foil reels.

## Summary of the Invention

A foil reel mounting device for supporting a stamping foil reel in a supporting module is disclosed. The device features a support provided with a recess dimensioned to receive the axle of the reel, together with a biased retaining element that is capable of moving between a closed position and an open position in order to secure or release the axle. This design, which is applicable to supporting modules and stamping machines alike, enables simplified loading and unloading of stamping foil reels through the automatic biasing mechanism that retains the axle in place.

## Detailed Description

The foil reel mounting device comprises a support member that forms the principal structural element for receiving the stamping foil reel. Formed within this support is a recess, or seat, shaped to accommodate the axle upon which the foil is wound. When the reel is presented to the mounting device, its axle is guided into the recess, where it comes to rest in a defined position that establishes proper alignment for the subsequent unwinding of the foil.

Cooperating with the recess is a retaining element that is arranged to move between two operative states. In the closed position, the retaining element extends across or partially over the opening of the recess, thereby capturing the axle and preventing it from being inadvertently withdrawn. In the open position, the retaining element is displaced clear of the recess opening, allowing the axle to be freely inserted into or removed from the seat.

A key feature of the device is the biasing of the retaining element. A biasing means—such as a spring or comparable resilient component—urges the retaining element toward the closed position. As a result, once an axle has been seated within the recess, the retaining element automatically returns to its closed position and holds the axle securely, without requiring any additional action on the part of the operator. During loading, the incoming axle may momentarily displace the retaining element toward the open position against the biasing force; once the axle passes into the recess, the biasing force drives the retaining element back to the closed position to lock the axle in place. Conversely, during unloading, the operator need only overcome the biasing force to move the retaining element to the open position, whereupon the axle can be lifted out.

## Application to Supporting Modules and Stamping Machines

The mounting device described above is particularly well suited for incorporation into a supporting module, which may carry one or more such devices to support one or more stamping foil reels simultaneously. Such supporting modules may in turn be integrated into a stamping machine, where they supply foil to the stamping station during operation.

By combining a simply configured recess with an automatically biased retaining element, the invention eliminates the need for cumbersome manual locking procedures. The self-actuating nature of the retaining mechanism ensures that reels are held reliably during operation while remaining readily interchangeable. This streamlined arrangement reduces machine downtime associated with reel changes and contributes to more efficient and user-friendly stamping operations.

# The Power of Small Words: "The" and "Also"

In the vast landscape of the English language, some of the smallest words carry the greatest weight. Two such words—"the" and "also"—demonstrate how essential brevity can be to clear communication.

## The Definite Article: "The"

"The" holds the distinction of being the most frequently used word in the English language. As the only definite article, it points to specific, known nouns rather than general ones. Consider the difference between "a book" and "the book." The former refers to any book, while the latter identifies a particular one already known to the reader or listener.

This tiny word performs remarkable work. It helps us:

- Specify unique objects (*the sun, the moon*)
- Reference previously mentioned items (*I saw a dog. The dog barked.*)
- Denote whole categories (*the tiger is endangered*)

Despite its brevity, "the" provides the structure that shapes our sentences.

## The Connective: "Also"

"Also" serves a different but equally valuable purpose. This adverb adds information, linking ideas together and signaling that something additional is being included.

For example: "She studied biology. She also studied chemistry."

The word "also" smoothly connects thoughts, indicating similarity or addition. It can appear at various points in a sentence, offering writers flexibility. Writers can also use it to build lists, emphasize points, or extend arguments without repetition.

## Conclusion

Together, "the" and "also" illustrate an important truth: significance is not measured by length. These small words also remind us that mastering the fundamentals of language—the articles, the connectives, the humble building blocks—is essential for anyone who wishes to communicate with clarity and precision.

# Patent Abstract

## Foil Reel Mounting Device for a Stamping Machine

A foil reel mounting device (10) for a stamping machine, configured to support and controllably dispense a stamping foil reel (12) during a hot foil stamping operation. The device comprises a mounting shaft (14) rotatably supported by a bearing assembly (16) affixed to a frame member (18) of the stamping machine. A foil reel core (20) is releasably secured to the mounting shaft (14) by a plurality of radially expandable locking members (22) which engage an inner surface of the reel core (20) upon actuation of a clamping mechanism (24).

A tension control assembly (26), operatively coupled to the mounting shaft (14), includes a friction brake (28) and a biasing element (30) that cooperate to maintain a substantially constant foil tension as the effective diameter of the foil reel (12) decreases during use. A sensor (32) disposed adjacent the foil path (34) monitors foil tension and transmits a signal to a controller (36), which adjusts the friction brake (28) accordingly.

The mounting shaft (14) is provided with a quick-release coupling (38) permitting rapid replacement of a depleted foil reel (12) without the use of tools, thereby reducing machine downtime. A guide roller (40) directs the dispensed foil (42) from the reel (12) toward a stamping die (44). The device (10) improves stamping accuracy, minimizes foil wastage, and facilitates efficient reel changeover in high-speed stamping operations.

# Technical Abstract

## Apparatus and Method for Mounting Stamping Foil Reels

An apparatus for mounting a stamping foil reel is disclosed, comprising a support configured to receive an axle about which the stamping foil reel is rotatably journalled. The support defines a recess dimensioned to seat the axle, the recess being open along one side to permit lateral insertion and withdrawal of the axle in a direction transverse to its longitudinal extent.

A biased retaining element is associated with the support and is movable between a retaining position, in which the retaining element extends at least partially across the open side of the recess to captively retain the axle therein, and a release position, in which the retaining element clears the open side to permit removal of the axle. The retaining element is urged toward the retaining position by a biasing means, such that the axle may be introduced into the recess by displacing the retaining element against the biasing force, whereupon the retaining element automatically returns to secure the axle without requiring separate fastening operations.

The support forms part of a supporting module adapted to be mounted within a stamping machine, the supporting module positioning the mounted reel to supply or receive stamping foil relative to a stamping station of the machine. The supporting module may accommodate one or more reels, including a supply reel and a take-up reel, and cooperates with the foil transport path of the stamping machine.

A method for loading and unloading a stamping foil reel is further disclosed, comprising the steps of: displacing the biased retaining element from the retaining position toward the release position; introducing the axle of the reel laterally into the recess through the open side; releasing the retaining element such that the biasing means returns it to the retaining position to secure the axle; and, for unloading, displacing the retaining element to the release position and withdrawing the axle laterally from the recess. The apparatus and method enable rapid, tool-free exchange of stamping foil reels, thereby reducing machine downtime and simplifying operator handling.
